notes: Jacked out of a Tread Lightly run on an advanced remote that then scored, clicked for credits for turns while holding 10-19 credits, and spent the final turn clearing tags instead of contesting the advanced Witch Hunt that won the game.
Simple but sensible install-advance-score loop out of a single iced remote with decent economy cards; protection stayed thin but the opponent never tested it.

Ran the same R&D top card three or four times every turn, sat on 3 credits installing nothing, and let the Corp score repeatedly from a one-ice remote, including the winning agenda while holding 9-12 credits.

Economy cratered to 0-2 credits for many turns, leaving HQ open (Architect Deployment Test stolen) and Megaprix in a remote behind non-ETR Drafter; Ansel and Tithe on the scoring remote eventually locked the Runner out.
Built a rig and stole three remote agendas, but spent long stretches in low-credit drip with repetitive HQ Docklands runs while the Corp scored twice, and paid 4 credits to clear harmless tags.

Installed agendas into a remote it could not afford to rez (Megaprix, Superconducting Hub stolen) with HQ open holding Méliès, then left R&D behind a lone Vertigo for ten turns while stacking ice elsewhere, losing to an R&D steal.
Solid economy and breaker setup, a timely remote steal and steady HQ/R&D pressure won the game; it stayed tagged throughout, which was only safe because the Corp was broke.
Repeated R&D runs on the same card, then clicked for credits for 15+ turns up to 76 credits without installing anything while the Corp advanced and scored five agendas largely unchallenged.
Mitosis put Lotus Haze in a naked remote where it was stolen, HQ stayed behind one unrezzed ice while agendas piled up there (three stolen), and the economy bottomed out at 0-2 credits.

Repeated the naked Mitosis install (Lotus Haze stolen), left Longevity Serum behind a single cheap ice against a 26-credit Runner, and let an agenda end up in open Archives, which gave the Runner the winning steal.
Efficient install-and-advance scoring with tag economy; the remote stayed on a single Ping against a rich Runner, which was risky but went unpunished.
Used Banner to bypass Akhet and kept up R&D pressure that won the game; it went broke early, which let one remote agenda score uncontested.
Clicked for credits early instead of developing, and with the Runner at 5 points installed Tomorrow's Headline behind a single Paywall, handing over the game.

Good opening (Jailbreak, Transfer of Wealth, Archives steal), then spent whole turns re-running a one- or two-card HQ while the Corp advanced Longevity Serum behind a non-ETR Diviner it had already passed.
Quick, purposeful win: set up breakers, stole from HQ, used Carpe Diem on Archives for Fujii, and checked R&D right after the Corp stacked it.
Iced an empty remote four deep but never installed an agenda in it, kept agendas in an HQ guarded only by Ablative Barrier (four stolen), and clicked for credits with 9-12 credits and a full hand.
Strong tempo: double Sure Gamble, Gachapon into Banner, and relentless HQ runs through Akhet won in four turns.
Spent ice and credits double-icing an Urtica Cipher trap and an empty remote while centrals had one non-ETR ice each, went broke, and let Flower Sermon land in open Archives for the losing steal.
An early Ansel on HQ locked the Runner out of steals, and Seamless Launch, Tranquility and Architect Deployment Test chained remote scores efficiently; the remote ice was light.

Stole 5 points early, then kept running HQ through F2P at 1 credit, piling up tags it spent the rest of the game clearing for 2 credits each, never reinstalled Gauss, and could not contest the scoring remote.
